Jesse —

Thanks for the clear questions and the attachments. Quick answers up front:

- Passback calculations for marketplace channel split are applied to the net revenue that Redwood reports to the marketplace after the private-offer discount is recognized (not the public list price).
- Marketplace fees and marketplace holdbacks are deducted before the reseller passback (so reseller % is on net after marketplace fees). Taxes are handled per region and are excluded from the passback base.

Folks — adding the operational details Ben -> (oops, that's me).

Concrete operational notes:

- On the marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure) private-offer flows, the revenue we report to the marketplace is the discounted private-offer amount. That becomes the basis for any partner/reseller passback we commit to. In short: list-price anchoring is just a storefront artifact; calculations use the private-offer net.

- Marketplace service fees (the platform cut) are deducted by the marketplace before we receive funds — accounting treats that as a fee and we calculate reseller % on the net cash we record. Example: Public list price $100k, private-offer committed price $60k, marketplace fee 5% => passback base = $60k - (marketplace fee on $60k). Reseller takes % on that base.

- Holdbacks: sometimes we model a small refund reserve (1–3%) to cover chargebacks/refunds; that reserve is typically taken from Redwood's net before passing through to resellers. We can make this explicit in the PO if Acme wants the reserve removed or capped.

- Taxes: we always exclude taxes from passback calculations and will follow tax treatment per jurisdiction.

Operational ask for Acme: if your reseller needs a line-by-line breakout on the settlement we can provide a partner settlement stub showing: gross private-offer amount, marketplace fee, refund reserve (if any), reseller passback. Let us know if you want that attached to the invoice or delivered as a separate monthly statement.

I'll attach a sample settlement stub in the morning.

Jesse — copying the template language so procurement has exactly what they'll see on the PO/invoice.

Invoice / settlement language (editable):
- "Private Offer Amount": final agreed amount for the private-offer as recorded by the marketplace.
- "Marketplace Fee": fee charged by the marketplace (deducted prior to Redwood remittance).
- "Refund Reserve": optional credit holdback (standard 1% unless otherwise agreed).
- "Reseller Passback": % of net remitted revenue after Marketplace Fee and Refund Reserve; taxes excluded.

If Acme needs the Refund Reserve removed or capped we can: (A) strike it and accept slightly delayed settlement terms, or (B) keep the 1% reserve but contractually guarantee a timely reconciliation and payout window (30 days after month close).

I can also confirm: we will not use the public list-price as the calculation base — everything is computed off the private-offer net.
